ugc_model.description: Full UGC campaign system: brands post campaign briefs, UGC creators apply, submit deliverables, receive payment on approval. This is module 8 of 16 in the PRD. Zero implementation exists.
ugc_model.implementation_note: No UGC-related pages, components, schema tables, API routes, or backend logic. Entirely greenfield.

campaign_lifecycle.description: The five-stage UGC campaign lifecycle from creation to completion

stages.description: Brand creates campaign brief with title, description, requirements, budget, per-creator pay, max creators, deadline, target platforms, and style guide. Campaign starts in draft status.
rules: Campaign must have at least one target platform
per_creator_pay_cents must be > 0
budget_cents must be >= per_creator_pay_cents * max_creators
deadline must be at least 7 days in the future for active campaigns
Business must have Stripe Connect account connected before activating

stages.description: Campaign published to UGC marketplace. UGC creators browse, filter, and apply with pitch and portfolio. Brand reviews applicants and accepts/rejects.
outputs: ugc_application records with status transitions: pending -> accepted | rejected
rules: Applications close on application_deadline or when max_creators accepted
Brand can view creator profile, portfolio, and past campaign ratings before deciding
Rejected creators receive notification with optional feedback
Accepted creators receive brief details and any product shipping info

stages.description: Accepted UGC creators produce and submit content deliverables. Brand reviews each submission against brief requirements.
outputs: ugc_deliverable records with status transitions: submitted -> approved | rejected | revision_requested
rules: Creator can submit multiple deliverables per campaign (up to deliverable_count limit)
Each deliverable is reviewed independently
Brand can request revision with specific feedback text
Maximum 3 revision requests per deliverable before auto-escalation
Deliverables must be submitted before campaign deadline

stages.description: Brand approves final deliverables. Approved content becomes available for brand use under agreed content rights.
rules: Approval is per-deliverable, not per-creator
Approval triggers payment processing automatically
Brand receives download links for approved content
Content rights transfer per the campaign's rights agreement (see content_rights section)

stages.description: Payment released to UGC creator's connected Stripe account via Stripe Connect transfer. Platform takes service fee.
rules: Payment is per approved deliverable at per_deliverable_rate_cents
Performance bonus added if bonus_performance_rate_cents set and conditions met
Platform service fee deducted before transfer (rate TBD — see open_questions)
Payment processed within 48 hours of approval
Creator must have connected Stripe Express account to receive payment

content_rights.description: Content rights management for UGC deliverables. Industry standard is that brands receive usage rights on approval, but specifics vary. This section codifies the rights model.
content_rights.open_question: OPEN_QUESTION_OPERATOR_DECISION_REQUIRED — What content rights model does CreatorOS enforce? Options below.

options.description: Brand owns all rights to approved content. Creator retains no usage rights. Standard for most UGC platforms.
cons: Creators may push back — limits portfolio use.

options.description: Brand receives perpetual license to use content in marketing. Creator retains ownership and can display in portfolio. Platform specifies allowed usage types per campaign.
cons: More complex. Need license terms per campaign.

options.description: Rights terms set by brand per campaign. Campaign brief includes rights_type field: full_buyout | licensed_perpetual | licensed_time_limited | portfolio_only.
pros: Flexible. Brands choose based on needs.
Different campaigns can have different terms.
cons: Complexity. Creators must read each campaign's terms.

content_rights.recommended_note: Per-campaign rights gives maximum flexibility. Campaign brief includes rights_type and rights_details fields. Platform provides standard templates for each rights type. Creator sees rights terms clearly before applying.

rights_fields.name: rights_details
rights_fields.note: Human-readable rights terms displayed to creators

rights_fields.name: rights_duration_days
rights_fields.note: For licensed_time_limited: number of days brand can use content

rights_fields.name: rights_acknowledged
rights_fields.note: Creator acknowledges content rights before applying

rights_fields.name: content_rights_granted
rights_fields.note: Set to true on brand approval — rights transfer confirmed

bidding.description: Bidding strategies for ad delivery optimization

strategies.label: Automatic (Recommended)
strategies.description: Platform optimizes bids to maximize results within budget. Best for most advertisers. No manual bid setting required.
strategies.note: Default for new campaigns. Platform sets bids based on competition and predicted performance.

strategies.label: Manual CPC (Cost Per Click)
strategies.description: Advertiser sets maximum cost per click. Platform optimizes delivery within that CPC cap.
strategies.note: Best for traffic and conversion campaigns where clicks are the primary goal.

strategies.label: Manual CPM (Cost Per 1,000 Impressions)
strategies.description: Advertiser sets maximum cost per 1,000 impressions. Platform delivers to maximize reach within CPM cap.
strategies.note: Best for awareness campaigns where impressions are the primary goal.

strategies.label: Target CPA (Cost Per Acquisition)
strategies.description: Advertiser sets target cost per conversion. Platform optimizes to hit that CPA. Requires conversion tracking setup.
strategies.note: Best for performance campaigns. Requires sufficient conversion data for optimization (minimum 50 conversions recommended).

auction_model.description: Second-price auction. Winner pays $0.01 more than the second-highest bid. Standard industry model.
auction_model.note: Actual implementation may use Vickrey auction variant. Exact auction mechanics are implementation detail.

controls.name: campaign_budget
controls.description: Total lifetime budget for the campaign. Campaign pauses when depleted.

controls.name: daily_budget
controls.description: Maximum spend per day. Platform smooths delivery across the day. Optional — if not set, campaign budget used with platform pacing.

controls.name: ad_set_budget
controls.description: Budget per ad set for granular control. Sum of ad set budgets must not exceed campaign budget.

controls.name: billing_threshold
controls.description: Advertiser charged when spend reaches threshold or at end of billing period, whichever comes first.

minimum_spend.open_question: OPEN_QUESTION_OPERATOR_DECISION_REQUIRED — What is the minimum campaign budget and daily budget? Options: $5/day (Meta-like, accessible), $10/day (YouTube-like), $1/day (aggressive, small-advertiser friendly). See open_questions section.

billing_model.description: Prepaid billing. Advertiser funds account balance or provides payment method. Charges drawn from balance as spend occurs.
billing_model.note: Stripe for payment processing. Same Stripe account as commerce, different flow.

ad_formats.description: Five ad format types corresponding to CreatorOS placement surfaces. Each format has specific creative requirements and is displayed natively within its placement context.

formats.label: Feed Ad
formats.description: Sponsored post in the consumer feed. Looks like a regular post with 'Sponsored' label. Supports image, video, and carousel. Highest reach format.
formats.example: Skincare brand showing product image in feed with 'Shop Now' CTA linking to external store

formats.label: Story Ad
formats.description: Full-screen vertical ad between stories. Auto-plays. Swipe-up CTA. High engagement format optimized for mobile.
formats.example: Fitness app showing 15-second workout clip with swipe-up to download

formats.label: Community Sponsorship
formats.description: Sponsored placement within community channels. Pinned message or sidebar banner within relevant communities. Highly targeted by community niche.
formats.targeting_note: Can target specific communities or community categories. High-intent audience — members actively engaged in niche.
formats.example: Developer tool sponsoring a coding community with pinned announcement and sidebar banner

formats.label: Course Promotion
formats.description: Promoted course listing in course discovery and search results. Boosted visibility for creator courses or external educational products.
formats.targeting_note: Target by course category, student interests, enrollment history. Can promote own courses (creator self-serve) or external courses (advertiser).
formats.example: Creator promoting their advanced photography course to students enrolled in beginner photography courses

formats.label: Product Boost
formats.description: Boosted product listing in marketplace search results and discovery. Increases visibility for creator products. Similar to Etsy Ads or Amazon Sponsored Products.

creative_specs.note: No custom creative required — uses existing product listing data (title, image, price). Advertiser only sets bid and budget.

formats.targeting_note: Automatic targeting based on product category, search keywords, and buyer behavior. No manual targeting needed.
formats.example: Creator boosting their Lightroom presets pack to appear at top of marketplace search for 'photo presets'

format_selection_guidance.note: Platform recommends formats based on campaign objective during creation wizard.

competitive_analysis.description: Competitive positioning of CreatorOS UGC and Ads against existing platforms

vs_aspire.what_they_do: Influencer discovery, campaign management, content approval, payment processing. Enterprise-focused. $2K+/mo pricing.
creatoros_advantages: Integrated into creator ecosystem — UGC creators are already on CreatorOS building their business
Built-in creator reputation from platform activity (not just self-reported metrics)
Lower cost: platform fee per campaign, not $2K/mo SaaS subscription
UGC content can be used directly in CreatorOS ads platform (closed loop)
Creators can transition from UGC work to building their own audience/products on same platform
creatoros_disadvantages: No existing creator database — Aspire has millions of indexed creators
No cross-platform analytics — Aspire integrates with social platforms for verified metrics
No established brand trust — Aspire has enterprise case studies

vs_meta_ads.what_they_do: Largest self-serve ads platform. Sophisticated targeting, massive reach, advanced ML optimization, full-funnel attribution.
creatoros_advantages: First-party data from actual purchases, enrollments, and community activity (no cookie dependency)
Creator niche targeting — reach audiences by the creator they follow, not just interest categories
Lower minimum spend accessible to small businesses and individual creators
Native UGC pipeline: source content AND run ads on same platform
Community sponsorship format — no equivalent on Meta (groups ads limited)
creatoros_disadvantages: Tiny audience compared to Meta's billions of users
No ML-optimized bidding (v1 will be rule-based)
No cross-platform tracking or attribution network
No brand safety tools, no third-party verification
Advertisers won't move budget from Meta to unproven platform without proven ROI

vs_youtube_ads.what_they_do: Video-first ads platform. Pre-roll, mid-roll, display. Google's targeting data. Massive video audience.
creatoros_advantages: Story and feed ad formats optimized for short-form mobile content (not pre-roll interruptions)
Course promotion format — directly target learners (YouTube has no equivalent)
Product boost format — marketplace ads like Etsy, not available on YouTube
Creator self-serve: creators can boost their own products without ad agency knowledge
creatoros_disadvantages: No video hosting scale — YouTube has 2B+ monthly active users
No Google search integration or Display Network reach
No TrueView format (skip after 5s) — proven engagement model
Limited advertiser tooling compared to Google Ads suite

competitive_analysis.positioning_summary: CreatorOS ads platform is NOT competing with Meta or Google for ad budgets. It's a niche, high-intent advertising surface for the creator economy. Competitive advantages are first-party data, creator-niche targeting, UGC pipeline integration, and accessible self-serve for small creators/businesses. Initial market: creators boosting their own products, small brands targeting creator audiences, UGC brands wanting closed-loop sourcing+promotion.

current_code.description: Zero implementation exists for either UGC Campaigns or Ads Platform

open_questions.question: What is the platform service fee percentage for UGC campaigns? Is it tiered by creator pricing tier (8%/5%/3% like marketplace), flat, or different?
open_questions.impact: Directly affects platform revenue model and creator economics. Must be decided before UGC payment flow implementation.
options: Same as marketplace: 8% Free tier, 5% Pro, 3% Business
Flat 10% for all UGC transactions (higher because platform provides matching service)

open_questions.question: What content rights model does CreatorOS enforce for UGC deliverables? Full buyout, licensed usage, or per-campaign configurable?
open_questions.impact: Affects creator willingness to participate, brand expectations, and legal terms. See content_rights section for full analysis.

open_questions.question: Does the brand fund the full campaign budget upfront, or does the platform charge per approved deliverable?
open_questions.impact: Affects cash flow, refund policy, and platform risk. Upfront funding is safer for creators but requires larger initial commitment from brands.
options: Full upfront: brand funds total budget at campaign creation. Unused refunded on completion/cancellation.
Pay-as-you-go: brand charged per approved deliverable. Payment method on file required. Higher risk of non-payment.
Hybrid: brand funds first batch of payments upfront. Additional charges as more deliverables approved.
open_questions.recommended_note: Full upfront ensures creators always get paid. Platform holds funds. Lower risk. Standard in UGC marketplace platforms.

open_questions.question: How are ads reviewed before going live? Automated, manual, or hybrid?
open_questions.impact: Affects ad quality, brand safety, time-to-live, and operational cost.
options: Automated only: keyword filter + image classifier. Fast but lower quality.
Manual only: human reviews every ad. High quality but slow and expensive.
Hybrid: automated filter catches obvious violations, human reviews flagged ads. Standard approach.
open_questions.recommended_note: v1 ships with automated keyword/image filter only (low operational cost at low volume). Add manual review queue when ad volume justifies it.

open_questions.question: What are the minimum campaign budget and daily budget for the ads platform?
open_questions.impact: Affects advertiser accessibility. Lower minimums attract small creators/businesses but increase operational cost per dollar of ad revenue.

options.label: Aggressive ($1/day)
options.note: Most accessible. Attracts individual creators boosting products. Low revenue per advertiser.

options.label: Standard ($5/day)
options.note: Meta's minimum. Balanced. Sufficient for optimization algorithms.

options.label: Premium ($10/day)
options.note: YouTube's minimum. Filters out lowest-value advertisers.

open_questions.recommended_note: Standard $5/day matches industry expectation. Low enough for individual creators, high enough for meaningful delivery.

open_questions.question: Does CreatorOS share ad revenue with creators whose content/audiences are being targeted? Or does the platform keep 100% of ad revenue?
open_questions.impact: Major strategic decision. Revenue share incentivizes creators to build audiences on CreatorOS. No share maximizes platform revenue.
options: No share: platform keeps all ad revenue. Standard for most platforms in early stage.
YouTube model: share % of ad revenue with creators whose content has ads placed. Requires significant ad volume to be meaningful.
Community sponsor share: community owners receive % of community_sponsorship ad revenue. Incentivizes community building.
open_questions.recommended_note: No revenue share at launch (insufficient volume for meaningful payouts). Introduce community sponsorship revenue share once ad volume proves the model. YouTube-style revenue share is a v3+ consideration.

open_questions.question: How are disputes handled when a brand rejects deliverables that the creator believes meet the brief?
open_questions.impact: Affects creator trust and brand satisfaction. No dispute resolution means creators bear all risk.
options: No formal dispute: brand's decision is final. Standard in most UGC platforms.
Platform mediation: creator can escalate to platform team. Platform reviews brief vs deliverable.
Escrow with auto-release: if brand doesn't review within N days, payment auto-releases to creator.
open_questions.recommended_note: Auto-release after 7 days protects creators from ghost brands. Optional platform mediation for disputes. Builds creator trust.

implementation_priorities.description: Recommended build order for UGC and Ads modules

phases.label: UGC Campaign MVP
phases.description: Core UGC campaign workflow: create, apply, submit, approve, pay
dependencies: Stripe Connect integration (shared with marketplace commerce)
File upload infrastructure (shared with content distribution)

phases.label: UGC Reputation + Content Rights
phases.description: Creator reputation system, content rights management, invite-only campaigns
scope: Creator reputation profile (ratings, badges, completion metrics)
UGC content performance tracking (external platform integration)

phases.label: Ads Platform MVP
phases.description: Basic ads platform: campaign creation, feed_ad and product_boost formats, auto bidding, basic analytics
scope: Campaign creation wizard (objective, targeting, budget, creative)
Feed ad and product boost formats only (highest value, lowest complexity)
Auto bidding only (no manual bid strategies)
Ads dashboard with spend and CTR metrics
dependencies: Consumer feed exists (for feed ad placement)

phases.label: Ads Platform Advanced
phases.description: Full targeting, all ad formats, manual bidding, conversion tracking, custom audiences
scope: Story ad, community sponsorship, course promotion formats
Manual CPC, CPM, target CPA bidding strategies
Custom audience creation (email list, website pixel, lookalike)

implementation_priorities.note: UGC should be built before Ads. UGC is simpler (workflow management vs ad serving infrastructure), provides immediate value (brands get content), and generates the content that can later be used in ads (closed loop).

eos_boundary.description: Boundary between EOS (business operations) and CreatorOS (creator product/distribution/community) for UGC and Ads
eos_handles: Business entity management (the business that runs UGC campaigns or ads)
Financial reporting and accounting for UGC spend and ad revenue
Tax compliance (1099s for UGC creators above threshold)
Pipeline management for ad sales (enterprise/managed accounts)
creatoros_handles: UGC campaign creation, management, and lifecycle
Ad campaign creation, targeting, and optimization
Ad serving and placement within CreatorOS surfaces
integration_points: Stripe Connect: shared infrastructure between EOS commerce and CreatorOS UGC/Ads payments
Business entity: UGC campaigns and ad campaigns link to businesses managed in EOS
Revenue signals: UGC payments and ad spend emit signals consumed by EOS financial reporting
